newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Beijing Datang Power says to offer 1.24 bln H-shrs.
newsitem.headline: Beijing Datang Power says to offer 1.24 bln H-shrs.

text.p: China's Beijing Datang Power Generation Co Ltd said on Monday it will offer 1.244 billion new H-shares in its flotation at a price ranging from HK$2.22 to HK$2.52 each.

The company said in its listing prospectus that of the new issue, 627.01 million H shares will be placed with professional and institutional investors, 492.65 million with New World Infrastructure Ltd and the remaining 124.41 million H shares will be offered to the public in Hong Kong.
H-shares are shares of mainland Chinese companies listed in Hong Kong.
The public offering in Hong Kong will run from March 11 to 14, and dealing in shares on the London and Hong Kong stock exchanges was expected to commence on March 21, the company said.
Morgan Stanley Asia Ltd is the global coordinator, sponsor and lead manager of the issue.
Datang Power operates coal-fired electric power plants which supply electricity to Beijing and other industrial cities in northern China.
The company estimated its profit after taxation for the year ended December 31, 1996, would be not less than 920 million yuan.
For the December 1997 year, it forecast that after-tax profit would be 1.10 billion yuan.
The company recorded a profit of 829 million yuan for the year ended December 1995, 798.2 million yuan for the 1994 year and 739.8 million for the 1993 year.
The prospectus 1997 price-earnings multiple based on the new issue price of HK$2.52 per H share will be 12 times on a fully diluted basis, and 11.5 times on a weighted average basis.
The adjusted net tangible assets per share is 1.67 yuan.

The company said the net proceeds of the H share offer of about HK$2.995 billion, of which HK$700 million would be used for the purchase of the first phase of the Zhang Jia Kou power plant in Hebei province, HK$862 million would be used to fund the construction cost of phase II of Zhang Jia Kou.

The company also said HK$1.2 billion would be used to fund the construction cost of the first phase of its Tuoketuo power plant and HK$222 million would be used to fund construction of its Dou He Second power plant.
